findings.issue: Killed its own shell ~9 times with a pgrep/pkill pattern that matches the invoking bash's own command line; diagnosed the cause early (turn 53) but kept re-running the same pattern
findings.suggestion: Use an exact-match kill (`pkill -f 'dist/server/entry\.mjs$'`, or `pgrep -x node` plus a filter) or kill by recorded PID; a one-line fix would have saved ~9 wasted command invocations

findings.issue: Attempted two edits against misremembered file contents; the files on disk were already correct (both edit calls failed)
findings.suggestion: Read (or grep) the exact current text before editing rather than trusting recollection of just-written files

findings.issue: Compared screenshots against a stale cached stylesheet for ~3 rounds, briefly misdiagnosing it as the build dropping media queries / an unchanged content hash
findings.suggestion: After a rebuild, force a cache-bypassing reload before screenshot comparison, and prefer `grep -o | wc -l` over `grep -c` on minified one-line bundles

findings.issue: No `astro check`/typecheck was ever run (typechecks: 0); correctness relied entirely on the Playwright suite
findings.suggestion: Add `astro check` to the loop to catch type/prop mistakes the acceptance tests may not exercise

summary: A well-run session: requirements and data were validated against the tests before any code, the app was built in one coherent pass, and the one hard failure (harness probe refused) was root-caused with a textbook minimal-repro experiment. Verification was exemplary — three full suite runs with the last after the final edit, plus per-page desktop/mobile screenshots compared to the design references, which surfaced real bugs the tests miss. The main blemish is a self-inflicted pgrep/pkill pattern that killed its own shell ~9 times and was never durably fixed.
